HTTP 200, 67 bytes, verbatim and complete: 'User-Agent: *' / 'Allow: /' / blank / 'Sitemap: http://royaldesign.com/sitemap.xml'. That is the ENTIRE file. ONE HOST ONLY - every request in this pass went to royaldesign.com (www.royaldesign.com 301s to the same origin); no API host, no CDN host, no proxy and no r.jina.ai was used, so no second robots check was owed. Both prior validated passes for this company used the /eu/ (English) storefront: Furniture.xlsx holds 58 royaldesign.com/eu/ furniture leaves and Final.xlsx holds the /eu/ lighting and home-decor leaves. I stayed on /eu/ so the dedup index stays URL-exact and so the Bathroom rows join the existing RoyalDesign records on the same locale. The authoritative figure is the storefront's OWN server-side payload that the PLP renders from: window.__INITIAL_STATE__.productsContainer['<path>'].totalProducts, alongside totalPages and the variants array of product ids. No number was taken from JSON-LD numberOfItems, from a nav attribute or from a meta description - the three traps named in the brief - and none was estimated, inferred or reused from a parent. VERIFICATION - EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION, not a spot check. For every node whose figure appears anywhere in this file I walked ?page=1..totalPages, concatenated the variants arrays and counted UNIQUE ids. Every single one matched totalProducts exactly, with no paging repeats and no shortfall: soap dispensers 109 = 48+48+13 across 3 pages, 109 unique; toothbrush holders 56 (2 pages) 56 unique; toilet brushes 69 (2) 69; laundry baskets 80 (2) 80; toilet roll holders 32 (1) 32; soap dishes 21 (1) 21; towel racks & holders 18 (1) 18; parent Bathroom Décor 382 (8) 382; room/bathroom 38 (1) 38; handtowels 448 (10) 448; bathroom rugs 76 (2) 76; shower curtains 33 (1) 33; bathrobes 22 (1) 22; bathroom lighting 72 (2) 72; mirrors 271 (6) 271; storage baskets 336 (7) 336; waste bins 171 (4) 171; soaps 35 (1) 35.
